**Source 1:** *The Hindu*  
**Title:** "Chandrayaan-3 lander module generated ‘ejecta halo’ on lunar surface during landing: ISRO study" (published 27 October 2023) [1]  
**Claim ID:** c1  
**Summary:** The report notes that the Indian Space Research Organisation's (ISRO) Chandrayaan-3 lander module, Vikram, successfully made a soft touchdown near the Moon's south pole on 23 August 2023 [1]. It reports that the landing made India the fourth country to achieve a lunar soft landing and the first nation in history to land in the lunar polar region [1].

**Source 2:** *The Guardian*  
**Title:** "India lands spacecraft near south pole of moon in world first" (published 23 August 2023) [2]  
**Claim ID:** c1  
**Summary:** The article reports that Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander successfully touched down shortly after 6:00 p.m. IST on 23 August 2023 near the Moon's south pole [2]. It highlights that the touchdown made India the first country to land a spacecraft near the lunar south pole [2].

**Source 3:** *BBC News*  
**Title:** "Chandrayaan-3: India makes historic landing near Moon's south pole" (published 23 August 2023) [3]  
**Claim ID:** c1  
**Summary:** The outlet reports that Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander made a historic touchdown at 18:04 local time on 23 August 2023 [3]. It confirms that India became the first space mission to successfully land in the lunar south pole region, as well as the fourth country overall to soft-land on the Moon [3].

**Source 4:** *Space.com*  
**Title:** "India on the moon! Chandrayaan-3 becomes 1st probe to land near lunar south pole" (published 23 August 2023) [4]  
**Claim ID:** c1  
**Summary:** The publication documents that ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 spacecraft executed a successful soft touchdown near the lunar south pole at 6:03 p.m. Indian Standard Time on 23 August 2023 [4]. It notes that this achievement made India the first nation to land near the lunar south pole and the fourth country to achieve a soft lunar landing [4].
